newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Tsumeb strike talks on hold until next week.
newsitem.headline: Tsumeb strike talks on hold until next week.

text.p: Negotiations to resolve a three-week-old strike at Gold Fields Namibia Ltd's Tsumeb operations in northern Namibia are on hold until next week after the union requested a postponement, the company said.
"The company put a proposal to the union yesterday at mediation and the union has asked for a postponement in the mediation," a company spokesman told Reuters by telephone from Namibia on Friday.
"They want to go back to their members and said they would get back to the mediators by next Friday (September 20)...the strike carries on."
Gold Field Namibia's Tsumeb Corp Ltd (TCL) mines and smelters have been shut down since August 23 when Mineworkers' Union of Namibia members took control of key areas.
The company regained control of all mine and smelter operations at Tsumeb on Wednesday, allowing 1,000 non-striking workers to return to work to carry out assessment work.
But production remains at a standstill with some 1,500 workers still out on strike, the spokesman said.
The strike is costing TCL some 80 tonnes a day in lost copper production and a similar amount in lost lead.

The company said its copper smelter was extensively damaged and was likely to take six to eight weeks to repair. The lead smelter did not appear to be damaged but will still take two to three weeks to restart.
TCL produced just under 30,000 tonnes of blister copper last year and 27,000 tonnes of lead. Most of the lead was produced from bought-in material while copper output was from TCL mines.
